rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes epsilon from 1e-8 to 1e-2 in the L2 norm computation. When the sum of squares of input elements is very small (near or below 1e-8), the epsilon term dominates the square root calculation. With original epsilon 1e-8, a small-norm vector produces scale≈1/sqrt(1e-8)≈10000. With mutated epsilon 1e-2, the same vector produces scale≈1/sqrt(1e-2)≈10. This 1000x difference in scaling is easily detectable. The mutation survived initial testing only because random inputs typically have much larger norms where the epsilon difference is negligible.
rounds.kill_strategy: Use a near-zero tensor with only tiny values so that sum-of-squares ≈ 1e-8 or smaller. This makes the epsilon term (1e-8 vs 1e-2) the dominant factor in the norm calculation, producing vastly different scale factors and output values.
rounds.recommendations: Add mutation testing coverage for epsilon guards using near-zero inputs. Different epsilon magnitudes (1e-8 vs 1e-2) require inputs with correspondingly small norms to expose behavioral differences.
